status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: OpenAI reported resolution of its ChatGPT/Codex incident. Reporting also records recovery of Claude and Grok. These restorations demonstrate repair of the affected services. The result covers the reported recoveries, not future resilience or a shared technical cause.

conclusion_change.previous: Three major frontier-AI service providers experienced overlapping availability failures on the same day. The available evidence gives different provider-specific explanations: OpenAI attributed its disruption to a routing error, Anthropic to an infrastructure issue, and xAI to an outage at its Memphis compute centre. The coincidence is relevant to resilience, concentration, dependency and correlated-failure analysis, but it does not establish a shared cloud, network, control-plane or infrastructure dependency. The separate provider causes are preserved and temporal overlap is not promoted into proof of a common dependency. All clauses resolve without governance mapping; degraded availability alone does not establish verifier failure, leverage or a required-control state. No eligible local or independently identified canonical duty is established.
